summary.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR945 crores (record Q1), but EBITDA margin slipped to 7.4% from 7.7% and PAT fell 20%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached a record INR945 crores, up 11% YoY in value and 3% in volume. EBITDA grew 6% to INR70 crores, with margin down 30 bps to 7.4%; PBT was broadly flat and PAT fell 20% on higher current tax. Gross profit rose 11% to INR258 crores with gross margin stable at about 27.3%, which management attributed to calibrated pricing and mix. Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi; 61% of revenue) saw volume fall 2% YoY, with B2C growing and B2B declining modestly; new-age business (Pride of Cows and Avvatar) grew 59% and reached about 13% of revenue.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY; gross margin stable (27.3% vs 28% in Q4 FY26 per call)

segments.name: Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi)
segments.commentary: 61% of Q1 revenue; volume down 2% YoY on transient slowdown in certain channels, value up 10%. B2C grew strongly while B2B declined modestly; B2C flagship growth was 'high single digit to close to double digit'. Dahi now included in flagship (previously in Others).

segments.name: New-age business (Pride of Cows, Avvatar)
segments.commentary: Grew 59% YoY, about 13% of revenue vs 9% a year earlier. Portfolio expanded into protein bars, ready-to-drink (RTD) coffee with 15 g protein per serving (launched Q1), creatine. Management said new-age margins are roughly double the company average, without giving a figure.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Down 46% YoY per analyst question; management said this reflects PSI and state incentive income falling after GST cut on ghee and cheese from 12% to 5% in September 2025, plus dahi moving into flagship. UHT and beverages performed reasonably well.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 revenue growth above 10%, with Q2 and Q3 supported by festive demand.
Calibrated price increases will continue in response to commodity costs; ghee prices were raised late in Q1 and new-age prices were revisited recently.
Milk prices described as stable; slight increase possible in coming months due to monsoon-linked seasonality and festive demand.
Distribution target of more than 1.5 million outlets within three years.
Management aspires to return flagship B2C growth to double digits; B2B will be pursued where margins allow.
capex_capacity: Cheese capacity to double from 60 to 120 metric tons per day over about 1.5 years, targeted by March 2028.
Doubling cheese capacity to be paired with a parallel expansion in whey protein generation; milk procurement to be scaled up to match.
Renewable energy: a solar JV with Tata Power Solar; biogas power from farm (about 5,000 cattle); the investment value was INR4.6 crores per the annual report, not INR50 crores.
demand_pricing: Whey protein prices reportedly moved from about INR2,500/kg to about INR3,400/kg recently; management said global whey demand is structural, not temporary.
Management said Avvatar retail prices rose only in stages, not 100% as an analyst suggested; consumers switch between protein formats as prices change.
Q1 B2B volumes were deliberately forgone where customers negotiated hard on pricing, to protect margins.
Avvatar sales are 75% via quick commerce, e-commerce and website, and 25% via traditional retail and specialised protein outlets.
Management said Google searches and website traffic rose about 200% over the last two months, after the India's Got Latent association.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth break the roughly 10% sales growth band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will exceed 10%, with Q2 and Q3 festive quarters expected to drive it; Q1 is seasonally weak.

qa_highlights.question: How is Avvatar up 59% when retail prices reportedly doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume also grew strongly and that prices rose in stages, not 100%; new products and lower-cost protein entry formats contributed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin flat despite mix improvement and price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said milk cost pass-through was complete in Q1 at INR42/litre, and the mix gain was offset by milk inflation; gross profit growth matched revenue growth at 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are core-category volumes falling despite wider distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is in B2B, where volumes were given up to protect profitability; B2C is not declining.

qa_highlights.question: Can B2B channel losses be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name customers or channels or give numbers, citing commercial sensitivity; B2B deals are short-term and come and go.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Samay Raina / India's Got Latent deal's cost and ROI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost, timeline or ROI, calling it a special commercial deal aimed at awareness.

qa_highlights.question: Is Avvatar's whey price rise a margin hit given backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost of production per kg or margin impact by product, saying margins are reported on a blended basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income spike in alternate quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income is usually higher in March due to annual fair-value gains on biological assets (cattle); Q1 FY26 also had a one-off gain on sale of the idle Sonipat plant.

risks_watch: Flagship volume decline (-2%) and B2B channel losses; watch whether B2C growth reaches double digits and offsets B2B.
EBITDA margin at 7.4% vs 7.7%, with brand media spend and Q1 seasonal absorption; watch for operating leverage in Q2 and Q3.
Tax-driven PAT decline (-20%); the current tax impact needs to be explained in future quarters.
Milk price stability versus monsoon and festive demand pressure, and dependence on price hikes for pass-through.
Other income is volatile (March fair-value gains; prior-year one-off), so the normalised base is unclear.
Cheese capacity doubling by March 2028 needs matching milk procurement.
Management declined to disclose new-age margin, category cost or Avvatar market share, limiting verification.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and brand strategy, but guarded on specifics: management repeatedly declined to disclose customer, channel, cost, ROI or market-share detail. It was defensive on margins, citing blended accounting and the seasonal Q1 absorption effect.
key_quotes: We delivered our highest ever Q1 revenue of INR945 crores, representing 11% year-on-year value growth and 3% volume growth.
As a result, the gross profit increased by 11% to INR258 crores, in line with the overall revenue growth, demonstrating that the cost push has been passed on.
So certainly, this year, we'll be breaking this 10% growth benchmark.
We are not degrowing on the B2C part of the total business.
